meanings.en: to accuse, to blame someone for a fault
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to accuse'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'accusé').

examples.text: Pourquoi accuses-tu notre patron cette nuit?
examples.trans: Why do you accuse our boss tonight?

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas un drame affreux.
examples.trans: That is not an awful drama.

meanings.note: Des animaux dans les bois. Masculine noun ('le animal', plural 'les animaux') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'animal'.

examples.text: Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois?
Une rivière qui coule? Des animaux qui gambadent dans les bois?
examples.trans: A flowing river? Animals frolicking in the woods?

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
Avoir besoin de = to need. Masculine noun ('le besoin', plural 'les besoins') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'need'.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je ne dors plus et je fais des cauchemars.
examples.trans: I no longer sleep and I have nightmares.

examples.text: Toute cette histoire ressemble à un cauchemar.
examples.trans: This whole affair resembles a nightmare.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.

examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: no preposition: chercher du travail

meanings.en: aller chercher = to go and get, fetch
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to look for'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'cherché').

examples.text: J'ai un petit loft. Et je cherche du boulot.
examples.trans: I've got a little loft. And I'm looking for work.

meanings.note: Chez moi: at my place. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Chez le docteur. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.trans: We went back to my place.
Really work on it at home.

meanings.note: Comment ça va?. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.
Informal. Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem. Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'.

examples.text: Faites-moi confiance, Audrey. Beyoncé a fait ça après son concert.
examples.trans: Trust me, Audrey. Beyoncé did that after her concert.

meanings.note: J'étais dans les sous-vêtements. Core French preposition meaning 'in', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Dans une heure = in an hour. Core French preposition meaning 'in', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film

examples.text: Tu l'as embrassée devant tout le monde!
examples.trans: You kissed her in front of everyone!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le drame', plural 'les drames') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drama'.

meanings.en: faire un drame = to make a big fuss
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le drame', plural 'les drames') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'drama'.

examples.text: Ce n'est pas un drame, Cécile. C'est simple.
examples.trans: It's not a big drama, Cécile. It's simple.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to have dinner'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'dîné').

meanings.note: Dans une heure = in an hour. Feminine noun ('la heure', plural 'les heures') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'hour'.

meanings.en: s'intéresser à = to be interested in
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to interest'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'intéressé').

examples.trans: It's the isolation of the mother and the daughter that interests me.

meanings.note: parler à quelqu'un = to talk to someone
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to speak'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'parlé').

examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'mental stress, psychological pressure'.
